about: MUTATING — delete ONE live Talos UserVolumeConfig on one worker so Talos unmounts the volume and keeps its partition (infra/forge/retire-user-volume.sh <node> <volume> <plan_sha256>) through the forge's ops_talosctl door (the talosconfig David placed, infra/estate/ops-credentials.sh). Door 1 of the volume-move protocol David asked for on 88b35891 (david_steer_20261106_1559Z: 'our control should be sufficient to manage moving the workloads') and ordered on 2026-11-07 ~02:00Z, filed as backlog 412d504c: w-1's gate volume moves from the Kingston SNV3S1000G to a Micron 7400 PRO without a reboot, and node-converge can only add (it refuses a DRIFT), so the provisioned volume must leave the live config first; wipe-a-partition, node-converge and the gate-volume proof follow, each a door of its own. AUTHORISED PER RUN BY DAVID'S PASSKEY in design 17835005's shape, as node-converge and add-longhorn-disk are: it declares requires_approval with the read-only plan-a-user-volume-retirement (this script's --plan) as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey on the approvers list signs those bytes, and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan; the script re-renders and deletes nothing unless today's plan hashes to it. The live document is in the bytes, so a second run of an applied plan is refused: at most once. THE BOUND IS THE SCRIPT'S, NEVER A PARAM: a registry node whose role is talos-worker, with the cluster agreeing on its address and carrying no control-plane label (refused before any door opens); the node's declaration in the tree still names the volume and passes check-declared.sh --only-read-classes, and the live UserVolumeConfig DRIFTs from it in its diskSelector — the tree has stated the move (a MATCH is refused: retiring it would only provision it again on the same disk); Talos reads u-<volume> ready at /var/mnt/<volume> on a partition labelled u-<volume>; and no running pod on the node mounts the path, anything under it, or a path that holds it, judged by each container's effective host path (hostPath or bound PersistentVolume, plus subPath; an unresolvable subPathExpr refuses when its source is related; review f1d1c254) — a gate run in flight; the one exemption is Longhorn's instance-manager mounting host / whole (namespace, label longhorn.io/component=instance-manager and name prefix all required), only when no Longhorn disk on the node is, holds or sits under the path, read from nodes.longhorn.io (backlog 76c8b647) — or nothing is done (exit 78). THE WRITE is one talosctl patch machineconfig --mode=no-reboot whose patch is the one document apiVersion v1alpha1, kind UserVolumeConfig, name <volume>, $patch: delete: Talos's merge removes that document and nothing else, and refuses a change it cannot apply live; no partition, filesystem or other document is written. THE EFFECT IS READ BACK: every 5 s for up to 180 s, the live machine config through check-declared.sh (UserVolumeConfig[<volume>] ABSENT), Talos's volumestatus u-<volume> (gone) and discoveredvolumes for the partition (still labelled u-<volume>); only when all three hold is the effect line printed, naming the partition that still holds the data (partition, parent disk, label), and otherwise the run exits 1 saying the retirement is NOT proven. Timeout 600: the plan's reads again (up to ~300 s with a first image pull), the apply (60 s inside its container), and the script's own 180 s read-back, which gives its verdict before the runner's kill.
effect: ^retire-a-user-volume: [a-z0-9-]+ on [a-z0-9-]+ is retired with its data kept — read back: the live machine config holds no UserVolumeConfig [a-z0-9-]+, Talos holds no volume [a-z0-9-]+, and partition [/a-z0-9]+ on disk [/a-z0-9]+ still carries partition label [a-z0-9-]+ \(
